branch_provenance.syndrome: Subacute Progressive Respiratory and Vascular Compromise with Mediastinal Mass and Metastatic Features

state.case_summary: A 45-year-old man presented with recent-onset dry cough and exertional dyspnea. He had no significant past medical history. Initial contrast-enhanced CT of the chest revealed a 12 cm mass in the anterior superior mediastinum and multiple bilateral pulmonary nodules suggestive of metastatic disease. A few weeks later, he developed neck edema, distended neck veins, and facial plethora. Repeat CT confirmed invasion of the superior vena cava above the azygos vein and thrombus extending into the left brachiocephalic trunk. He was treated with heparin and high-dose corticosteroids, with rapid symptomatic relief; stenting was deferred. Video-assisted thoracoscopy yielded a wedge resection of a pulmonary lesion and biopsy of the mediastinal mass. Histopathology showed a multinodular proliferation of small, round, monomorphic cells with clear cytoplasm. Immunohistochemistry demonstrated diffuse strong WT1 positivity and moderate, patchy CD99 positivity.

excluded_candidates: Lymphoma: due to the presence of a mediastinal mass and metastatic disease, but the histopathology and immunohistochemistry results suggest a different diagnosis
Thymoma: considered due to the location of the mass, but the presence of WT1 and CD99 positivity points towards a different diagnosis
